# Prose inventory + register classification — GH#397 Phase 0/2 prep

**Generated by** `qa/scripts/extract_prose.py all --outdir docs/prose-naturalization`
(seed 397, deterministic — a re-run on the same tree is byte-identical).
**Acceptance criterion 3**, first half: *all player-facing map prose is
inventoried and classified*. The rewrites themselves are Phase 2's.

## 1. Corpus size

| corpus | strings | words | issue's blind audit |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| dialogue (`data/dialogue/*.json`) | 1,438 | 24,584 | 1,482 / ~24.5k |
| map prose (`data/maps/**/*.json`) | 847 | 19,041 | 825 / ~18.5k |
| **total** | **2,285** | **43,625** | — |

Word counts land within 0.5% (dialogue) and 3% (maps) of the issue's figures;
string counts differ by boundary convention (whether `"@bank"` reference
strings are counted — they are structure, and are skipped). `self-test` gates
both corpora against these ballparks, so a wrong field list fails loudly.

**Map prose field list** is derived by full key census, not assumption — see
the `extract_prose.py` header for per-field counts and every documented
exclusion. Two notes on scope:

- The whole toast family is matched by rule (`key == "toast"` or
  `endswith("_toast")`), so a future map's new toast key is picked up
  automatically rather than silently missed.
- `copy` (5 strings — the Guild board's readable notices) is player-facing
  prose that the issue's field enumeration did not name. Included.
- `display_name` (431) is excluded: player-facing, but a **name**, not prose.
- `talk_pool` / `talk_pool_stages` / `talk_banks` (~305 strings) are excluded
  as #388's closed register. Disjointness from that gate's walker is asserted
  in `self-test`, so the two issues cannot double-count or leave a gap.

## 2. Register distribution

Four registers per the issue's Phase 1. **`register` is the TARGET register**,
i.e. what the string's job in the game says it should sound like — not a
description of how it currently reads. The gap between the two is the work.

| region | strings | functional | scenic | character-bearing | landmark | demotion candidates |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| pallass | 149 | 42 | 91 | 16 | 0 | **16** |
| riverfarm | 134 | 34 | 91 | 9 | 0 | 7 |
| invrisil | 125 | 22 | 57 | 44 | 2 | 6 |
| liscor | 97 | 25 | 33 | 38 | 1 | 1 |
| floodplains | 89 | 29 | 54 | 5 | 1 | 7 |
| inn | 89 | 33 | 22 | 34 | 0 | 1 |
| dungeon | 61 | 20 | 31 | 8 | 2 | 8 |
| sewers | 48 | 15 | 30 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| ruin | 43 | 3 | 29 | 9 | 2 | 3 |
| garden | 12 | 1 | 11 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **total** | **847** | **224** (26%) | **449** (53%) | **165** (19%) | **9** (1%) | **50** |

**Demotion candidates** = a functional or scenic string whose final sentence
trips the button smoke score (≥2/5), excluding protected keeps and holdout.
This is the Phase 2 work queue: a string performing landmark register without
earning it. It is a queue to *read*, not a list proven wrong — the smoke score
is a detector, and `review-rubric.md` §4 says the read wins.

## 3. Method, and how far to trust it

Honest accounting, because a work order that overstates its own authority is
worse than one that doesn't.

**What is mechanical and reproducible.** Register is assigned by a documented
heuristic in `extract_prose.py:classify_row` — field type first (a
`skill_hint_toast` is functional because its job is to inform), then entity
kind (an `npc`'s `observe` is character-bearing), then evidence (a resolution
field that *banks quest progress* is landmark). Every string also carries a
one-word rationale tag naming which rule fired.

**What is hand-audited.**
- The **landmark tier in full, every row**, because it sets the scarcity
  budget. That audit changed the rule: the first version keyed landmark on
  field alone and swept in lift rides, guest cots and "Your own bed." — 16
  traversal/rest resolutions that are plainly functional. Landmark now
  requires a banked accomplishment, and 4 further corrections are recorded in
  `classification-overrides.json` with reasons.
- Functional / scenic / character-bearing were audited **by tag group, not row
  by row.** A sample of each tag was read; the rule was corrected where the
  sample was wrong (this is what moved 298 "banks an accomplishment" props out
  of character-bearing and into scenic — banking makes a prop
  *quest-load-bearing*, not *character-revealing*).

**What is not settled.** Individual scenic-vs-character-bearing calls on
`observe`/`toast` are the softest edge, and 847 rows have not each been
adjudicated. Phase 2 region lanes are expected to re-judge and **must record
the change in `classification-overrides.json`** rather than edit silently —
`self-test` fails on an override whose id does not bind, so a stale
correction cannot become a quiet no-op.

## 4. What the numbers say about the problem

These are the issue's six tell families, counted. They are the reason the
issue's blind audit rated map prose (94%) far worse than dialogue (78%).

| tell | map prose (n=847) | dialogue (n=1438) |
|---|--:|--:|
| anonymous-agent inference (`someone`/`somebody`/`whoever`/…) | 267 (**32%**) | 183 (13%) |
| button smoke ≥2/5 | 68 (**8%**) | 35 (2%) |
| negation/correction | 29 (3%) | 11 (1%) |
| `which from X is Y` / `the way X does` / `the X is the X` | 12 | 1 |
| CAPS emphasis | **23** | **0** |
| mid-line ellipsis | **6** | **0** |
| "the whole of / the entire" | **2** | **0** |

**The last three rows are the headline.** CAPS, ellipsis and "the whole of"
are *hard-banned in dialogue* and enforced at zero by
`dialogue_voice_gate.py`. Map prose fields are **not walked by that gate at
all**, and every one of those banned shapes is still alive there — including
the exact construction the issue quotes from `riverfarm_village.json`, "That
is the whole of Riverfarm's vocabulary for gratitude". The corpus is not
uniformly gated; it is gated in one register and unguarded in the other.

Nuance that matters for Phase 4: of the 23 CAPS instances, roughly 15 are
**diegetic lettering** — signage and notices being read (`COYLE AND SONS`,
`PERMIT AND STAMP REQUIRED`, `THE WANDERING INN`, `WATCH NOTICE`). Those are
legitimate; they render what is painted on the object. Only ~8 are emphasis
CAPS (`ANCHOR`, `CLICKS`, `POURING`, `HAND`, `SLEEP`, `RECOVERS`, `DOOR`,
`WITH`). Any map-prose CAPS gate must distinguish the two or it will fail 15
correct strings. Flagged `[ADJUDICATE]` in the bible draft.

### Anonymous-agent inference concentrates in the empty places

| region | strings with an anonymous agent |
|---|--:|
| garden | 7/12 (58%) |
| dungeon | 30/61 (49%) |
| ruin | 20/43 (47%) |
| sewers | 21/48 (44%) |
| floodplains | 29/89 (33%) |
| invrisil | 38/125 (30%) |
| pallass · riverfarm · inn · liscor | 26% each |

The ruins, sewers and dungeon — the locations with **nobody in them** — infer
the most invisible people. That inversion is tell family 3 at its clearest:
where there is no one to observe, the narrator supplies someone.

### Where the buttons are

`pallass` carries 16 of the 50 demotion candidates on 0 landmark strings — the
most over-authored region relative to its payoffs, matching the issue's
"Pallass generally: standards, forms, measurements, queues" motif note.
`dungeon` (8), `floodplains` (7) and `riverfarm` (7) follow. `inn`, `liscor`,
`sewers` and `garden` are close to clean.

## 5. Landmark scarcity, measured

**9 landmark strings across 847 (1.1%), in 7 of 30 map files.** The other 23
files carry none. Per file:

| file | landmark strings | beat |
|---|--:|---|
| `ruin/ruin_surface.json` | 2 | the plinth/Door retrieval (base + one variant of one beat) |
| `dungeon/trapped_halls.json` | 1 | the seal opening |
| `dungeon/seal_vault.json` | 1 | the Anchor (Act V payoff) |
| `invrisil/mercantile_alleys.json` | 2 | two distinct quest payoffs |
| `floodplains/floodplains.json` | 1 | the rift seam |
| `liscor/street.json` | 1 | the sewer grate |
| `sewers/sewers.json` | 1 | the fissure descent |

This is the empirical basis for the bible's scarcity budget: the corpus
already *spends* landmark register about once per payoff site, and the
problem is not the 9 — it is the 50 demotion candidates spending it a second
time where nothing was earned.
